Title: QumulusAI presenta domanda per quotazione diretta sul Nasdaq Da Investing.com

Summary: 
QumulusAI has filed a registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to pursue a direct listing on the Nasdaq Global Market, with the expected ticker symbol 'QMLS'. The filing covers the sale of all currently issued and outstanding common shares by existing shareholders. Shares held by directors, executives, and shareholders owning more than 10% of the company will be subject to a six-month trading restriction after the listing. Between January 1, 2025, and December 1, 2025, QumulusAI issued shares to investors at prices ranging from $1.00 to $3.60 per share. The company noted that these historical prices may not reflect broader market demand once trading begins. Unlike a traditional initial public offering (IPO), the direct listing will not involve investment banks underwriting the offering. Instead, existing shareholders may sell shares through market-based transactions at prevailing market prices. QumulusAI will not receive any proceeds from these sales. Chardan Capital Markets LLC serves as the financial advisor, responsible for determining when shares are ready for trading and approving the Nasdaq Current Reference Price, based on pre-market buy and sell orders. Currently, there is no public market for QumulusAI's common shares. The company warned that trading volume and price volatility could be higher than in a traditional IPO due to the innovative nature of direct listings. The registration statement did not specify the total number of shares registered for sale.

Published date: December 31 2025, 21:10

Title: Weekly Blockchain Blog - January 2026 #2

Summary: 
BitGo Holdings, Inc. announced its initial public offering (IPO) of 11,821,595 shares of Class A common stock, filing a registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The company provides digital asset infrastructure services, including custody, wallets, staking, trading, financing, and settlement via regulated cold storage. In related news, the U.S. arm of a major global bank launched a product enabling on-chain mirrored representations of client deposit balances on its private permissioned blockchain, with early participants including prominent financial institutions and digital natives. Meanwhile, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) issued a proposed rulemaking to clarify that national trust banks may engage in non-fiduciary activities, conditionally approving five national trust bank charters for digital asset-focused firms despite opposition from full-service banks. The proposal, informed by the GENIUS Act, aims to formalize longstanding authority and is open for public comment until February 11, 2026. On the legislative front, the U.S. Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs published four fact sheets outlining the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act, which seeks to combat illicit finance, protect consumers, provide regulatory clarity, and promote responsible decentralized finance innovation. The Senate Banking Committee postponed the bill’s markup on January 14, 2026, to allow for ongoing negotiations. In cybersecurity, researchers identified a supply chain attack via six malicious npm packages linked to the North Korean Lazarus Group, which were downloaded over 300 times and designed to steal credentials, install backdoors, and extract cryptocurrency data. Chainalysis released its 2026 Crypto Crime Report, revealing that illicit cryptocurrency addresses received at least $154 billion in 2025—a 162% year-over-year increase—driven by nation-state actors (e.g., North Korea’s $2 billion in thefts, Russia’s $93.3 billion in A7A5 token transactions), Chinese Money Laundering Networks (CMLNs), full-stack criminal infrastructure providers, and the growing use of crypto in violent crime, including physical coercion and human trafficking.

Published date: January 21 2026, 21:27

URL: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/weekly-blockchain-blog-january-2026-2-4777692/
Source: JD Supra
Classification: Technology
Sentiment: positive
Reporting voice: Objective
Continent: North America

Title: KRAKacquisition Corp Announces Filing of Registration Statement on Form S-1 for Proposed Initial Public Offering

Summary: 
KRAKacquisition Corp, a newly formed blank check company (SPAC) incorporated in the Cayman Islands, announced on January 12, 2026, the filing of a registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for a proposed initial public offering (IPO). The IPO is expected to consist of 25,000,000 units at $10.00 per unit, with each unit comprising one Class A ordinary share and one-fourth of one redeemable warrant. The company intends to list its units on the Nasdaq Global Market under the ticker symbol 'KRAQU.' Santander is serving as the sole book-running manager. The offering will be conducted exclusively through a prospectus, and preliminary prospectus copies may be obtained from Santander via email at equity-syndicate@santander.us, phone at 833-818-1602, or the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov. The registration statement has been filed but is not yet effective, and no securities may be sold until it becomes effective. KRAKacquisition Corp was formed to effect a business combination with one or more operating businesses, and is sponsored by an affiliate of Kraken. Forward-looking statements in the release include expectations about the IPO and the search for a business combination, with no assurance that the offering will close or that a business combination will be completed. Risks are detailed in the company’s SEC filings, available at www.sec.gov. The company undertakes no obligation to update these statements except as required by law.

Published date: January 12 2026, 22:42

URL: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/01/12/3217408/0/en/KRAKacquisition-Corp-Announces-Filing-of-Registration-Statement-on-Form-S-1-for-Proposed-Initial-Public-Offering.html
